evidence.claim: Karat Packaging describes itself as a manufacturer and distributor of single-use disposable products used in restaurant and foodservice settings, including containers, bags, boxes, tableware, cups, lids, cutlery, and straws.

Karat’s 2025 filing says it offers disposable foodservice products and related items, including take-out containers, cups, lids, gloves, janitorial supplies, and plant- or bio-based Karat Earth products, while noting California single-use-plastic regulatory changes.
Graphic Packaging’s Americas Paperboard Packaging segment includes cups, lids, and food containers sold primarily to foodservice companies and quick-service restaurants in the Americas.
Performance Food Group’s Foodservice segment serves independent and chain restaurants and offers disposables, cleaning and kitchen supplies, and related products in addition to food items.
Amcor and Berry announced a combination intended to strengthen positions in categories including food service, and the acquisition closed on April 30, 2025.
evidence.source_title: Amcor and Berry to combine in all-stock transaction

evidence.claim: Amcor reported that its all-stock acquisition of Berry Global was completed on April 30, 2025, with Berry businesses added to Amcor’s flexible and rigid packaging segments.
Pactiv Evergreen was delisted after being acquired by Novolex; this removes a formerly direct public foodservice-packaging comparable from the active US-listed universe.
evidence.source_title: Novolex and Pactiv Evergreen Complete Combination

evidence.claim: Sysco’s 2024 annual report disclosed paper and disposables sales of about $5.386 billion and equipment and smallwares sales of about $1.545 billion, confirming that non-food supplies are a meaningful foodservice-distribution category.

memory_update.text: KRT is the cleanest small-cap public pure-play candidate for restaurant packaging/disposables; prioritize in later layers for gross-margin durability, customer concentration, import exposure, and eco-compliant SKU pricing power.
GPK should remain in the universe as a mid-cap paperboard/QSR packaging candidate, but later layers must isolate foodservice exposure from broader CPG paperboard exposure.

Foodservice distributors such as PFGC and SYY are useful demand-signal anchors because their product categories include paper/disposables, equipment, smallwares, cleaning, and kitchen supplies, even when they are not manufacturers.

PTVE and Berry Global are no longer standalone public candidates after 2025 consolidation: PTVE was acquired by Novolex and delisted; Berry was acquired by Amcor. This reduces the number of direct public pure plays and may increase the importance of KRT and GPK as listed comparables.

node: Restaurant supplies, packaging, tableware, napkins, cups, and disposables
summary: Layer 1B expands the public-market universe for restaurant packaging and disposables. The cleanest underfollowed direct exposure found is Karat Packaging, a small-cap manufacturer/distributor of single-use disposable foodservice products. Graphic Packaging is a mid-cap paperboard and foodservice packaging supplier with QSR exposure but broader CPG exposure. Performance Food Group is a large-cap distributor/context anchor because its foodservice segment sells disposables, cleaning and kitchen supplies to restaurants. Amcor is a large-cap reference name after acquiring Berry Global, giving it broader foodservice packaging scale, but the exposure is less pure and more widely followed. Pactiv Evergreen would have been a strong direct reference name, but it was acquired by Novolex and delisted on April 1, 2025, so it is excluded from candidates and retained as a coverage-gap memory item.
